title: Provincial minimum wage (Upah Minimum Provinsi, UMP) by province, Indonesia, 1997-2025: BPS figures, with Ministry of Manpower (Kemnaker) figures for the years BPS does not publish

columns.province_code: BPS province code (kode_bps) of the 38 provinces; there is no Indonesia row (see 'national_rows'). Names and Kemendagri codes in 'provinces'.
columns.period: YYYY, the year the minimum wage is set for; a UMP applies to the whole calendar year from 1 January.
columns.status: Revision marker; no source gives one, so every row is empty (see notes on dataset 473's '2022*').
columns.value: Rupiah per month: whole rupiah in the years from BPS, and up to 2 decimals, as Kemnaker stores them, in the years from Kemnaker (see 'sources').

province_source.note: BPS and Kemendagri codes differ for the six Papua provinces; join other datasets on the code system they use.

minimum_wage.name: Upah Minimum Provinsi (UMP), provincial minimum wage; BPS labels it 'Upah Minimum Regional/Propinsi', naming the older term UMR beside UMP
minimum_wage.definition: Upah Minimum adalah upah bulanan terendah berupa upah tanpa tunjangan atau upah pokok termasuk tunjangan tetap yang ditetapkan oleh gubernur sebagai jaring pengaman.Upah Minimum Provinsi yang selanjutnya disingkat UMP adalah Upah Minimum yang berlaku untuk seluruh kabupaten/kota di dalam wilayah 1 (satu) provinsi.
minimum_wage.definition_english: The minimum wage is the lowest monthly wage, being the wage without allowances or the basic wage including fixed allowances, set by the governor as a safety net. The UMP is the minimum wage that applies to every regency and city within one province.
minimum_wage.unit: rupiah per month (BPS unit 'Rupiah'; Kemnaker '(Rp)', and 'upah bulanan' in its definition)
minimum_wage.decimals: 0 in the BPS years; up to 2 in the Kemnaker years, shown by Kemnaker with the format #,##0.00
minimum_wage.source: see 'sources': BPS WebAPI var 220 where BPS publishes the year, Kemnaker Satu Data otherwise

sources.statement: Every value of 1997-2016 and 2018-2020 is BPS's (WebAPI var 220). The values of 2017 and 2021-2025 are not BPS figures: BPS publishes none for those years, so they come from the Ministry of Manpower (Kementerian Ketenagakerjaan, Kemnaker) Satu Data portal. This departs from the project's practice of using BPS numbers only, by the user's choice. BPS's own note names Kemnaker as its source ('Sumber: Kementerian Ketenagakerjaan').
sources.rule: Each year takes all its values from the first source in this order that holds the year; the lower-priority copies serve as checks (checks.cross_source). Kemnaker's datasets repeat only 2018-2020 (36 and 473), all BPS years, and 473, the later release, ranks above 36.

kemnaker_36.role: gives every value of 2017; checks 2016 and 2018-2020 against BPS
kemnaker_36.title: UMP Nasional Tahun 2016-2020
kemnaker_36.abstract: Dalam kurun waktu 5 (lima) tahun terakhir telah terjadi peningkatan rata-rata UMP nasional sebesar 35,82 persen atau sekitar Rp 704.798,77 dari Rp 1.967.572,00 pada tahun 2016 menjadi Rp 2.672.370,77 pada tahun 2020. Dlihat dari nilai UMP yang ditetapkan oleh masing-masing provinsi, rentang nilai UMP di Indonesia cenderung mengalami peningkatan sejak tahun 2016 – 2020. Pada tahun 2016 rentang nilai UMP di Indonesia berada pada rentang nilai Rp 1.312.355,00 – Rp 3.100.000,00 dan kini pada tahun 2020 telah meningkat menjadi Rp 1.704.608,25 – Rp 4.276.349,91.

periods.note: One value per province and year: the year the UMP is set for, as BPS's tahun and Kemnaker's titles and year columns name it. A UMP is set by the governor before the year starts and applies from 1 January.

gaps.21 2002: BPS var 220 holds no value for Kepulauan Riau in 2002-2004, between its values for 1997-2001 and from 2005, and no Kemnaker file covers those years
gaps.21 2003: BPS var 220 holds no value for Kepulauan Riau in 2002-2004, between its values for 1997-2001 and from 2005, and no Kemnaker file covers those years

gaps.34 2016: neither source gives a 2016 value: BPS var 220 has no key, and Kemnaker dataset 36 prints '-'

coverage.formed_note: 'formed' gives the year each later province was formed, which is general knowledge, not read from these files. BPS var 220 lists several of them from 1997 or 1998, before they were formed, mostly with the value of the province they were formed from ('years_equal_to_parent'); the values are kept as BPS publishes them.
coverage.kalimantan_utara: BPS var 220 starts Kalimantan Utara (65) in 2015, with Kalimantan Timur's value; its note says the 2013 figure is still combined with Kalimantan Timur ('Data Kalimantan Utara tahun 2013 masih bergabung dengan Kalimantan Timur'), and the files give no 2014 value either.
coverage.new_papua_provinces: Kemnaker dataset 1611 (2024) is the first file to list Papua Barat Daya (92), Papua Selatan (95), Papua Tengah (96) and Papua Pegunungan (97), as its abstract says ('termasuk upah minimum bagi provinsi baru di Indonesia'); dataset 942 (2023) lists only Papua Barat (91) and Papua (94).

borders: A UMP is a rate set for a province, not a total over its area, so a value does not change because the province's area changes; still, a change of a province from the year before is left out of the change checks when a province formed from it gains or loses its own value that year (checks.change_not_compared).
91 (Papua Barat) and 94 (Papua) up to 2023 are the UMPs of the pre-split provinces; the four new Papua provinces have their own values from 2024.

national_rows.decision: The dataset has no Indonesia (00) row. Indonesia has no national minimum wage: each source's national row is an average of the provincial UMPs, a derived value that belongs in analysis/. Kemnaker labels its row 'Rata-rata' (average) and computes it as the unweighted mean of the provinces it lists; BPS's INDONESIA row is not described by BPS and, in every year but 2014, is such a mean over a set of provinces that changes from year to year (checks.identities).
national_rows.formula: unweighted mean (Rp per month) = sum of minimum_wage over the provinces with a value that year / the number of those provinces

notes: Sources by year: 1997-2016 and 2018-2020: BPS WebAPI var 220; 2017: Kemnaker Satu Data dataset 36; 2021-2022: Kemnaker Satu Data dataset 473; 2023: Kemnaker Satu Data dataset 942; 2024: Kemnaker Satu Data dataset 1611; 2025: Kemnaker Satu Data dataset 2252. Every value of 2017 and 2021-2025 is a Kemnaker figure, not a BPS figure.

Where BPS and Kemnaker hold the same year (2016, 2018-2020), BPS's whole-rupiah values equal Kemnaker's rounded to whole rupiah, within 0.5 rupiah, except Jawa Barat 2016 and Banten 2019 (checks.cross_source, declared_differences). The two Kemnaker releases 36 and 473 agree exactly in 2018-2020.

Jawa Barat (32) 2016: BPS publishes 2,250,000, Kemnaker dataset 36 1,312,355. BPS's figure equals its own 2016 value for Sulawesi Selatan (73), and Kemnaker's abstract names 1,312,355 as the lowest UMP of 2016, so BPS's figure looks like an error; the CSV keeps it by the stated priority, and checks.flags lists the rise into 2016 and the fall into 2017 for a person to decide.

Jawa Barat, Jawa Tengah, DI Yogyakarta and Jawa Timur (32-35) have the same value in 2015 as in 2014 in BPS var 220, and BPS's own 2015 INDONESIA mean leaves these four out (checks.identities); neither source gives them a 2016 value (coverage.gaps). checks.flags lists the four unchanged 2015 values.

2021: dataset 473's abstract says most provinces set the same UMP as in 2020, under SE Menaker Nomor M/11/HK.04/X/2020, so 2021 values equal to 2020's are expected and the unchanged check does not read 2021.

Dataset 473 heads its 2022 column '2022*' with the note '*) data per 8 Februari 2022': the 2022 values are as Kemnaker recorded them on 8 February 2022. This is a date of record, not a BPS revision status, so the 2022 rows keep an empty status (source_tables.kemnaker_473.column_marker).

The series switches between BPS's whole rupiah and Kemnaker's decimals at 2016/2017, 2017/2018 and 2020/2021, so a change across a switch includes up to 0.5 rupiah of BPS's rounding: an unchanged 2021 UMP can show as a change of a few tenths of a rupiah.

Dataset 36 fills 2020 cells with two colours that its legend explains (source_tables.kemnaker_36.cell_notes): Nusa Tenggara Timur, Kalimantan Tengah, Gorontalo and Sulawesi Barat set their 2020 UMP under PP 78/2015 with the phased approach to decent living needs (KHL), and Bengkulu, Bali and Papua Barat not under PP 78/2015.
Derived values are not stored: change from the year before (%) = (value in year t / value in year t-1 - 1) x 100; the national mean is in 'national_rows'.

checks.flags lists every value, change and unchanged value outside its range in checks.plausible_ranges for a person to review, with the two values and their sources each change compares; a flag stays whether it reflects a real event or a source error.

identities.check: BPS var 220's INDONESIA row equals the unweighted mean of the provinces the file lists that year, with the declared exceptions; written to the metadata only
each Kemnaker average row (Rata-rata) equals the unweighted mean of the provinces its dataset lists, within 0.005 rupiah, and each average formula covers exactly the province rows of its column

The CSV keeps BPS's value by the stated priority, and checks.flags lists the changes into and out of 2016 for a person to decide
BPS writes 2,267,990 where both Kemnaker releases give 2,267,990.55: BPS dropped the decimals instead of rounding them to 2,267,991, a gap of under 1 rupiah

abstract_figures.check: every figure a Kemnaker abstract states equals the statistic of the dataset's own values, to 2 decimals

DI. YOGYAKARTA.reason: Kemnaker writes 'DI.' with a full stop, which normalise_name keeps

minimum_wage_rupiah.measure: every value, rupiah per month. The UMPs in these files run from 106,000 (1997) to 5,396,761 (2025), so a value below 100,000 or above 6,000,000 is a unit or digit error rather than a minimum wage

minimum_wage_change_pct.measure: (value in year t / value in year t-1 - 1) x 100. Below -0.001: the UMP fell (one rupiah of rounding where the series switches between BPS's whole rupiah and Kemnaker's decimals is under 0.001% of any UMP here). Above 50: a rise of more than half in one year, beyond the largest median rise across provinces in these files (32.4%, 2001)

unchanged_from_previous_year_rupiah.measure: |value in year t - value in year t-1|, rupiah. Below 1 rupiah the UMP did not change (allowing for the rounding at a switch of source); 2021 is not read, since dataset 473's abstract states the 2021 freeze
